title: Binary codes near distance 1/2: remove the logarithm
credit: Classical (MRRW 1977 gap); eps-biased formulation Alon et al. (1992)
premise_risks: 2026 MRRW improvements (OpenAI ch.2, Alrabiah-Guruswami, honeycomb arXiv:2608.20287 unrefereed) - checked numerically that kappa_H keeps the eps^2 log(1/eps) order, but the honeycomb bound's near-1/2 behaviour was not analysed in its abstract
Close to the belief that GV is tight (sometimes attributed to Goppa); this claim is strictly weaker
plain: Let A(n,d) be the largest number of binary strings of length n that pairwise differ in at least d positions. When d=(1/2-eps)n, random codes give about 2^{(2/ln 2) eps^2 n} strings, but the best upper bounds (the 1977 linear-programming bound and its 2026 refinements) give only 2^{O(eps^2 log(1/eps)) n}. Show that the logarithm is not needed: the rate is at most a constant times eps^2.
math: Let $A_2(n,d)=\max\{|C|:C\subseteq\{0,1\}^n,\ d_H(x,y)\ge d\ \forall x\ne y\in C\}$. Prove that there is an absolute constant $K$ such that for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1/4]$, $\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac1n\log_2A_2\!\left(n,\lceil(\tfrac12-\varepsilon)n\rceil\right)\le K\varepsilon^2$.
